sources.label: Spotify streaming history
sources.what: One listener’s complete extended streaming history — every play, with duration, skip and shuffle flags.
sources.caveat: The export documents its timestamps as UTC, but the hour histogram says otherwise: read as UTC and shifted to IST, listening peaks at 05:00 and all but stops at 17:00, which is nobody's day. Read as written, it peaks at midnight and empties at noon. They are already local, so they are used unshifted. 149,860 plays cannot ship to a browser, so the unit here is the listening session — consecutive plays less than 30 minutes apart. Searches are reconstructed from first appearances, not recorded.

sources.label: Household ledger
sources.what: A hand-kept daily expense ledger in INR, with free-text notes someone typed every day for four years.
sources.caveat: Dates are day-first with inconsistent padding and many rows carry no time at all; those are filed at midday and tagged time-unknown, and excluded from anything plotted against the hour. Places were already anonymised in the source as "Place 0"–"Place 5" and are preserved as written. Messages are reconstructed from transfers, not recorded.

sources.label: Card ledger
sources.what: An Indian card-transaction set built for fraud-detection research, carrying merchant, category, amount, city and a per-row fraud label.
sources.caveat: Its three identity columns do not agree on how many people are in it — 1,019 distinct customer ids, 1,330 distinct card numbers, 1,279 distinct names — and 230 of 917 customer ids carry more than one person's name. Nobody here has a usable personal timeline, so the layer is attributed to the archive owner as a whole. Every merchant carried a "fraud_" prefix as an artefact of the file's origin, which is stripped. Its fraud label is true on 5,046 of 10,267 rows — just under half, because the file was balanced for training a classifier — so a flagged charge here describes how the dataset was built, not something that happened to a person, and the app says so rather than dressing it up as a mystery. The geography is synthetic: of the 8,792 rows carrying coordinates, only 128 fall inside India, and 294 of 311 cities appear under more than one state, so the state column is not shipped and no map is drawn. City names are real and are used as written. No card number is shipped at all: the column was written out of a float, so it reaches the ETL either rounded to trailing zeros or printed as 4.42786e+18, and there are no last four digits left in it to keep.
